statements.text:
The required generic spectral interface is precisely

    e_* (Law_Q(B) restricted to {B>0}) <= sigma_m          (S)

as measures: every nonnegative measurable spectral test has the corresponding integral inequality. The matrix law is restricted before pushing it forward. It is a finite subprobability on the left, not a claim that sigma_m is normalized.

P(3.5) plus its symmetric-matrix Lebesgue change of variables in section 7 supplies (S) analytically: push forward the measure inequality

    Law_Q(B) <= C_0 exp(-c ||B||_F^2) dB.

Consequently

    W 1_depth <= A_m r^2 U^(2m) lambda_1(lambda_1+ErU)
                 1_{C_m, lambda_1<=DrU^2}.               (1)

E_Q[W;depth] <= integral_(J,x in T_n)
      r^2 P(x) U^(2m) integral_0^(DrU^2) t(t+ErU) dt
      dLaw(J) dx,                                       (2)

For n>=1, s>=0 and c>0, define

    G(n,s,c) = pi^(n/2) Gamma((n+s)/2)
               / [2^n n! Gamma(n/2) c^((n+s)/2)].        (3)

This is exactly the integral of ||x||^s exp(-c||x||^2) over T_n. Proof: the radial integrand assigns equal mass to the 2^n orthants and the n! coordinate-order chambers; their boundaries are Lebesgue null. Polar integration gives sphere area 2 pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2), while substitution y=c rho^2 contributes the factor 1/2 and Gamma((n+s)/2). These factors give (3). The 2^n n! factor applies AFTER radial domination; it is not a second factor in C_sp.

Since Lambda<=||x|| and (J+Lambda)^p<=2^(p-1)(J^p+Lambda^p), Tonelli and the probability normalization of Law(J) give

    E integral_Tn (J+Lambda)^p Lambda^v exp(-c||x||^2) dx
      <= 2^(p-1) [M_p G(n,v,c)+G(n,v+p,c)].              (4)

As U>=1, its spectral envelope is bounded using the single residual moment p=2m+6. A sufficient explicit constant is

    C_depth = C_sp A_m (D^3/3+ED^2/2) 2^(p-1)
              [M_p G(n,v,c)+G(n,v+p,c)].                (5)

Then E_Q[W;depth] <= C_depth r^5. If Z=E_Q W>=c_Z r^2 with c_Z>0, the actual weighted probability satisfies

    Q^W(depth) <= (C_depth/c_Z) r^3.                    (6)

On the near part h<=H J^2 with H=K(1+4D). Put E_s=3H/2. The bounded scalar density C_0 and independence of J from B imply

    E_Q[W;near depth] <= C_0 H^2/4
       * (64D^3/3+8E_s D^2) E J^10 r^5.                (8)

The far part is

    E_Q[W;far] <= (4D)^4 M_far r^6,
    M_far >= sup E_Q[(W/r^2)lambda^4].                  (9)

For E4 use exactly P(7.7), with M_4joint bounding E_Q[(W/r^2)M4^4] uniformly:

    Q^W(E4) <= M_4joint/[c_Z(3k_-/10)^4] r^4.

From ADAPTER_ENVELOPE.md line 13:
- m>=2, n=m-1, a probability law Q, 0<r<=1 and k>=k_->0.
- B=-A_M is a measurable real symmetric m x m matrix with increasingly ordered eigenvalues e(B).
- J>=1 is measurable and independent of the entire B, with E_Q J^p<=M_p for p=2m+6.
- W>=0 is integrable and W=0 off the typed support T. On T: B>0, h=M3>=0, h<=K(J+Lambda) with K>0 and Lambda=lambda_m, and P(6.2) holds.

Spectral reference measure (lines 15-24): sigma_m = C_sp exp(-c sum lambda_i^2) Delta(lambda) 1_{C_m} d lambda with c>0. The convention-dependent C_sp is not set to one (line 30).

Definitions (lines 36-41): U=J+Lambda, D=4K^2/(3k_-), E=3K/2, A_m=K^2(1+K)^(m-1)/4, v=m(m-1)/2. (2) uses T_n={0<x_1<=...<=x_n} and P(x)=C_sp A_m Lambda^v exp(-c||x||^2) (lines 61-63).

Further conditions:

- Uniformity requires K, k_-, C_sp, c, M_p and c_Z to be uniform over the fixed-dimension, fixed-torus, compact-mark, compact-frame family (line 97).

- Cap assembly (lines 127-135): the geometric cap implication 'W>0 and goodCap => G_geometric' must hold Q-almost everywhere where W>0, and both tails are divided by the same positive full Z.

theorem positive_chamber_lintegral (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (hG : Measurable G) :
    (∫⁻ l : ℝ × ℝ in {l | 0 < l.1 ∧ l.1 < l.2}, G l) =
      ∫⁻ T : ℝ in Ioi 0, ∫⁻ x : ℝ in Ioo 0 T, G (x,T) := by

theorem gaussian_depth_plane_eq (ν : Measure ℝ) (C0 c r K k0 : ℝ) :
    (∫⁻ j, (ENNReal.ofReal Real.pi *
      ∫⁻ l : ℝ × ℝ in {l | 0 < l.1 ∧ l.1 < l.2},
        ENNReal.ofReal (l.2-l.1) *
          (ENNReal.ofReal (C0*Real.exp (-c*(l.1^2+l.2^2))) *
            CapI4DepthKernel.depthKernel r K k0 (j,l))) ∂ν) =
    ENNReal.ofReal Real.pi * (∫⁻ j, (∫⁻ T : ℝ in Ioi 0,
      ∫⁻ x : ℝ in Ioo 0 T, ENNReal.ofReal (T-x) *
        (ENNReal.ofReal (C0*Real.exp (-c*(x^2+T^2))) *
          CapI4DepthKernel.depthKernel r K k0 (j,(x,T)))) ∂ν) := by

theorem gaussian_depth_plane_le (ν : Measure ℝ) [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (C0 c r K k0 : ℝ) (hC0 : 0 ≤ C0) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hK : 0 ≤ K) (hk0 : 0 < k0)
    (hsupp : ∀ᵐ j ∂ν, 1 ≤ j) (h9 : Integrable (fun j : ℝ => |j|^9) ν) :
    (∫⁻ j, (ENNReal.ofReal Real.pi *
      ∫⁻ l : ℝ × ℝ in {l | 0 < l.1 ∧ l.1 < l.2},
        ENNReal.ofReal (l.2-l.1) *
          (ENNReal.ofReal (C0*Real.exp (-c*(l.1^2+l.2^2))) *
            CapI4DepthKernel.depthKernel r K k0 (j,l))) ∂ν) ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (256*Real.pi*C0*(K^2*(1+K)/4)*
      (((4*K^2/(3*k0))^3/3)+((3*K/2)*(4*K^2/(3*k0))^2/2))*r^5*
      ((∫ j : ℝ, |j|^9 ∂ν)*(∫ T : ℝ in Ioi 0, T^2*Real.exp (-c*T^2)) +
        ν.real univ*(∫ T : ℝ in Ioi 0, |T|^11*Real.exp (-c*T^2)))) := by

theorem gaussian_depth_plane_lt_top (ν : Measure ℝ) [IsFiniteMeasure ν]
    (C0 c r K k0 : ℝ) (hC0 : 0 ≤ C0) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hK : 0 ≤ K) (hk0 : 0 < k0)
    (hsupp : ∀ᵐ j ∂ν, 1 ≤ j) (h9 : Integrable (fun j : ℝ => |j|^9) ν) :
    (∫⁻ j, (ENNReal.ofReal Real.pi *
      ∫⁻ l : ℝ × ℝ in {l | 0 < l.1 ∧ l.1 < l.2},
        ENNReal.ofReal (l.2-l.1) *
          (ENNReal.ofReal (C0*Real.exp (-c*(l.1^2+l.2^2))) *
            CapI4DepthKernel.depthKernel r K k0 (j,l))) ∂ν) < ∞ := by

items.title: Cap I4 d=3 eighth-moment depth bound by residual split rJ^2=1 (E_Q[W;A] <= (C_lo+C_hi) r^5, Q^W(A) <= (C_lo+C_hi)/cZ r^3) and dyadic countermodel against sub-eighth moments

statements.text:
E[W;A intersect B_lo]
      <= C_s a Bstar r^5 E_J integral_0^infinity
                           L^2 H(L) (J+L)^8 exp(-cL^2)dL
      <= C_lo r^5,                                      (L)

where

    C_lo = 128 C_s a Bstar *
      { M8[K I2(c)+(1+K)I3(c)] + K I10(c)+(1+K)I11(c) }.

Combining (L) and (T8) proves, under the explicit abstract hypotheses,

    E_Q[W;A] <= (C_lo+C_hi) r^5.                         (M8)

With the actual FULL normalizer Z=E_Q W>=cZ r^2, cZ>0, exactly one division gives

    Q^W(A) <= (C_lo+C_hi)/cZ * r^3.

For E4={3k/10<rM4}, keep the separate actual joint premise
E_Q[(W/r^2)M4^4]<=M4joint. It yields

    Q^W(E4) <= M4joint/[cZ(3k_floor/10)^4] r^4.

Let B have the full Gaussian entry density

    p(B)=(sqrt(2)/pi^(3/2)) exp(-||B||_F^2)

on symmetric 2x2 matrices. It is normalized in da db dd. Independently let J=2^n with probability

    p_n=(255/256)2^(-8n), n=0,1,... .

Thus J>=1, E[J^p]=(255/256)/(1-2^(p-8)) is finite for EVERY real p<8, while E[J^8]=infinity. In particular E[J^2]=85/84. Set h=J, k=4/3, K=1, and

    W_r=(r^2 J^2/4) lambda^2 L^2 1_{B>0}.

Choose r_N=2^(-(2N+1)). For every n<=N, r_N J^2<=1/2. Restrict the numerator to these n and to the displayed spectral rectangle; using L^2>=1 and integrating lambda^2 to r_N J^2 gives

    E[W_(r_N);depth]
      >= (gstar/12) r_N^5 sum_{n=0}^N p_n 2^(8n)
       = (gstar/12)(255/256)(N+1) r_N^5.

Hence

    Q^W_(r_N)(depth)/r_N^3
      >= [gstar/(12z0)](255/256)(N+1) -> infinity.

There is no uniform cubic bound despite all strictly sub-eighth moments being finite. This shows why a hypothesis asserting only moments of order below eight cannot generally replace the eighth-moment assumption within this broad comparison class. It does NOT say every individual model with infinite eighth moment fails, nor that the actual source field needs a heavy-tail analysis: P already supplies all finite residual moments. The new argument is a moment-sufficiency refinement, not an assertion of new field physics or literature priority.

theorem radial_positive_tonelli (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (hG : Measurable G) :
    (∫⁻ t : ℝ, ∫⁻ r : ℝ in Ioi 0, ENNReal.ofReal r *
      (if 0 < t-r then G (t-r,t+r) else 0)) =
      ∫⁻ q : ℝ × ℝ in {q | 0 < q.2 ∧ q.2 < q.1},
        ENNReal.ofReal q.2 * G (q.1-q.2,q.1+q.2) := by

theorem entry_spectral_radial (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (hG : Measurable G) :
    (∫⁻ e : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ), G (CapI4Polar.eigenvalues e)) =
      (2 : ℝ≥0∞) * ENNReal.ofReal (2*Real.pi) *
        ∫⁻ t : ℝ, ∫⁻ r : ℝ in Ioi 0,
          ENNReal.ofReal r * G (t-r,t+r) := by

theorem entry_positive_spectral_lintegral (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞)
    (hG : Measurable G) :
    (∫⁻ e : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ),
      if 0 < (CapI4Polar.eigenvalues e).1 then G (CapI4Polar.eigenvalues e) else 0) =
      ENNReal.ofReal Real.pi *
        ∫⁻ l : ℝ × ℝ in {l | 0 < l.1 ∧ l.1 < l.2},
          ENNReal.ofReal (l.2-l.1) * G l := by

theorem density_positive_spectral_bound
    (p : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) → ℝ≥0∞) (H G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞)
    (hH : Measurable H) (hG : Measurable G)
    (hdom : ∀ e, p e ≤ H (CapI4Polar.eigenvalues e)) :
    (∫⁻ e : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ), p e *
      (if 0 < (CapI4Polar.eigenvalues e).1 then G (CapI4Polar.eigenvalues e) else 0)) ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal Real.pi *
        ∫⁻ l : ℝ × ℝ in {l | 0 < l.1 ∧ l.1 < l.2},
          ENNReal.ofReal (l.2-l.1) * (H l * G l) := by

    (ν : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (R : Ω → ℝ)
    (r ε M : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hi : Integrable (fun x => R x ^ 4) ν)
    (hM : (∫ x, R x ^ 4 ∂ν) ≤ M) :

theorem double_soft_integral (a b : ℝ) :

theorem matrix_soft_integral (r D E U : ℝ) :
    (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..(D * r * U ^ 2), x * (x + E * r * U)) =
      r ^ 3 * ((D ^ 3 / 3) * U ^ 6 + (E * D ^ 2 / 2) * U ^ 5) := by

def spectralEnvelope (m : ℕ) (D E P U : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  P * U ^ (2 * m) * ((D ^ 3 / 3) * U ^ 6 + (E * D ^ 2 / 2) * U ^ 5)

noncomputable def spectralKernel (m : ℕ) (r D E P U : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  r ^ 2 * P * U ^ (2 * m) *
    (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..(D * r * U ^ 2), x * (x + E * r * U))

theorem spectral_kernel_eq (m : ℕ) (r D E P U : ℝ) :
    spectralKernel m r D E P U = r ^ 5 * spectralEnvelope m D E P U := by

def MatrixDepthTransport
    (μ : Measure Ω) (W lam M3 : Ω → ℝ) (k r : ℝ)
    (ν : Measure Ξ) (m : ℕ) (D E : ℝ) (P U : Ξ → ℝ) : Prop :=

    ∫ z, spectralKernel m r D E (P z) (U z) ∂ν

theorem depth_numerator_r5
    (μ : Measure Ω) (W lam M3 : Ω → ℝ) (k r : ℝ)
    (ν : Measure Ξ) (m : ℕ) (D E : ℝ) (P U : Ξ → ℝ) (M : ℝ)
    (ht : MatrixDepthTransport μ W lam M3 k r ν m D E P U)
    (hi : Integrable (fun z => spectralEnvelope m D E (P z) (U z)) ν)
    (hM : (∫ z, spectralEnvelope m D E (P z) (U z) ∂ν) ≤ M)
    (hr : 0 ≤ r) :
    (∫ x in depthEvent k r lam M3, W x ∂μ) ≤ M * r ^ 5 := by

    (μ : Measure Ω) (W lam M3 : Ω → ℝ) (k r : ℝ)

    (hr : 0 < r) (hcZ : 0 < cZ) (hM0 : 0 ≤ M)

    (ht : MatrixDepthTransport μ W lam M3 k r ν m D E P U)
    (hi : Integrable (fun z => spectralEnvelope m D E (P z) (U z)) ν)
    (hM : (∫ z, spectralEnvelope m D E (P z) (U z) ∂ν) ≤ M) :

    (hD : 0 < D) (hr : 0 < r) (hlam : 0 < lam)
    (hdepth : lam ≤ 2 * D * r * J ^ 2 + 2 * D * r * lam ^ 2) :
    lam ≤ 4 * D * r * J ^ 2 ∨ 1 / (4 * D * r) < lam := by

theorem scalar_soft_integral (r D E J : ℝ) :
    r ^ 2 * J ^ 4 *
      (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..(4 * D * r * J ^ 2), x * (x + E * r * J ^ 2)) =
        r ^ 5 * (64 * D ^ 3 / 3 + 8 * E * D ^ 2) * J ^ 10 := by

theorem scalar_far_fourth_moment
    (ν : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (lam : Ω → ℝ)
    (D r M : ℝ) (hD : 0 < D) (hr : 0 < r)
    (hi : Integrable (fun x => lam x ^ 4) ν)

    (ν {x | 1 / (4 * D * r) < lam x}).toReal ≤ (M / (1 / (4 * D)) ^ 4) * r ^ 4 := by

theorem cap_union_mass
    (ν : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (k r : ℝ) (lam M3 M4 : Ω → ℝ) :
    (ν (goodCap k r lam M3 M4)ᶜ).toReal ≤

def spectralPair : (ℝ × ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ × ℝ :=
  Matrix.toLin (.finTwoProd ℝ) (.finTwoProd ℝ) !![(1 : ℝ), -1; 1, 1]
theorem det_tracePair : LinearMap.det tracePair = -(1/2 : ℝ) := by
theorem det_spectralPair : LinearMap.det spectralPair = (2 : ℝ) := by

theorem tracePair_spectralPair (q : ℝ × ℝ) :
    tracePair (spectralPair q) = (q.1, -q.2) := by

theorem map_tracePair :
    Measure.map tracePair (volume : Measure (ℝ × ℝ)) = (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • volume := by

theorem map_spectralPair :
    Measure.map spectralPair (volume : Measure (ℝ × ℝ)) = (1/2 : ℝ≥0∞) • volume := by

theorem lintegral_tracePair (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (hG : Measurable G) :
    (∫⁻ q : ℝ × ℝ, G (tracePair q)) = (2 : ℝ≥0∞) * ∫⁻ q : ℝ × ℝ, G q := by

theorem lintegral_spectralPair (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (hG : Measurable G) :
    (∫⁻ q : ℝ × ℝ, G (spectralPair q)) = (1/2 : ℝ≥0∞) * ∫⁻ q : ℝ × ℝ, G q := by

theorem positive_chamber_change (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (hG : Measurable G) :
    (∫⁻ q : ℝ × ℝ in {q | 0 < q.2 ∧ q.2 < q.1}, G (q.1-q.2, q.1+q.2)) =
      (1/2 : ℝ≥0∞) * ∫⁻ e : ℝ × ℝ in {e | 0 < e.1 ∧ e.1 < e.2}, G e := by

theorem weighted_positive_chamber_change (G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (hG : Measurable G) :
    (∫⁻ q : ℝ × ℝ in {q | 0 < q.2 ∧ q.2 < q.1},
      ENNReal.ofReal q.2 * G (q.1-q.2, q.1+q.2)) =
      (1/4 : ℝ≥0∞) * ∫⁻ e : ℝ × ℝ in {e | 0 < e.1 ∧ e.1 < e.2},
        ENNReal.ofReal (e.2-e.1) * G e := by

items.hypotheses: volume is Lebesgue (Haar) measure on ℝ × ℝ. G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞ is measurable (hG). tracePair(a,d) = ((a+d)/2,(a-d)/2) and spectralPair(t,ρ) = (t-ρ,t+ρ) are linear maps given by explicit 2x2 matrices. The positive chamber is {0 < q.2 < q.1} in (t,ρ) and {0 < e.1 < e.2} in (λ,Λ). Integrals are nonnegative lower Lebesgue integrals, infinite values allowed, and no positive floor on the larger eigenvalue is used (README.md:25-29).

items.title: Cap I4 d=3 polar sub-bridge: ordered 2x2 eigenvalue coordinates, trace/determinant identities, nonnegative polar change of variables and anisotropic density-envelope bounds (CapI4Polar, unreplayed Lean)

statements.text: def radius (z : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (z.1 ^ 2 + z.2 ^ 2)

def spectrum (t : ℝ) (z : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  (t - radius z, t + radius z)

def traceCoordinates (e : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ)) : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  ((e.1 + e.2.2) / 2, ((e.1 - e.2.2) / 2, e.2.1))

def eigenvalues (e : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ)) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  spectrum (traceCoordinates e).1 (traceCoordinates e).2

theorem spectrum_product (t : ℝ) (z : ℝ × ℝ) :
    (spectrum t z).1 * (spectrum t z).2 = t ^ 2 - z.1 ^ 2 - z.2 ^ 2 := by

theorem spectrum_sq_sum (t : ℝ) (z : ℝ × ℝ) :
    (spectrum t z).1 ^ 2 + (spectrum t z).2 ^ 2 =
      2 * (t ^ 2 + z.1 ^ 2 + z.2 ^ 2) := by

theorem eigenvalues_product (e : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ)) :
    (eigenvalues e).1 * (eigenvalues e).2 = e.1 * e.2.2 - e.2.1 ^ 2 := by

theorem polar_spectral_lintegral (t : ℝ) (F : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) :
    (∫⁻ z : ℝ × ℝ, F (spectrum t z)) =
      ∫⁻ p : ℝ × ℝ in polarCoord.target,
        ENNReal.ofReal p.1 * F (t - p.1, t + p.1) := by

theorem density_polar_bound (t : ℝ) (p w F : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞)
    (hdom : ∀ z, p z ≤ w (spectrum t z)) :
    (∫⁻ z : ℝ × ℝ, p z * F (spectrum t z)) ≤
      ∫⁻ q : ℝ × ℝ in polarCoord.target,
        ENNReal.ofReal q.1 * (w (t - q.1, t + q.1) * F (t - q.1, t + q.1)) := by

theorem integrated_density_polar_bound
    (p : ℝ → ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (w F : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞)
    (hdom : ∀ t z, p t z ≤ w (spectrum t z)) :
    (∫⁻ t : ℝ, ∫⁻ z : ℝ × ℝ, p t z * F (spectrum t z)) ≤
      ∫⁻ t : ℝ, ∫⁻ q : ℝ × ℝ in polarCoord.target,
        ENNReal.ofReal q.1 * (w (t - q.1, t + q.1) * F (t - q.1, t + q.1)) := by

items.hypotheses: t ∈ ℝ and z ∈ ℝ × ℝ. The entry convention is e = (a,(b,d)) for [[a,b],[b,d]] (CapI4Polar.lean:21). F, p and w are arbitrary functions into ℝ≥0∞; no measurability hypothesis appears in the quoted integral statements. The density bounds assume the pointwise envelope hdom: ∀ z, p z ≤ w (spectrum t z), for every t in the integrated form. The polar side is the lintegral over Mathlib's polarCoord.target with radius factor ENNReal.ofReal p.1.

theorem torus_proj_isOpenQuotientMap (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L) :
    IsOpenQuotientMap (torus_proj d L hL) where

theorem closedSuperlevel_preimage (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
    (g : E d → ℝ) (hperiodic : IsLPeriodic d L g) (a : ℝ) :
    (torus_proj d L hL) ⁻¹'
        {q : torus_quotient d L hL | a ≤ descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic q} =
      {x : E d | a ≤ g x} := by

theorem quotient_closedSuperlevel_lpc_of_euclidean
    (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
    (g : E d → ℝ) (hperiodic : IsLPeriodic d L g) (a : ℝ)
    (hEuclideanLPC : LocallyPathConnectedSpace {x : E d // a ≤ g x}) :
    LocallyPathConnectedSpace
      {q : torus_quotient d L hL // a ≤ descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic q} := by

theorem quotient_death_attainment_of_euclidean_closedLPC
    (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
    (g : E d → ℝ) (hsmooth : IsSmooth d g) (hperiodic : IsLPeriodic d L g)
    (hmorse : IsMorseDistinct d L g) (M : E d)
    (hnonessential : ¬ superlevelBar_isEssential g M)
    (hEuclideanLPC : LocallyPathConnectedSpace
      {x : E d // superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ g x}) :
    ∃ Q ∈ quotientCriticalSet d L hL g,
      g M < descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic Q ∧
      ∃ γ : Path (torus_proj d L hL M) Q,
        (∀ t : unitInterval,
          superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic (γ t)) ∧
        ∃ t : unitInterval,
          descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic (γ t) = superlevelBar_deathHeight g M := by

statements.text:
**Chart `C_transverse` (d=2).** Fixed `1 < A < B < ∞`, witness coordinate `y=(y1,y2)` with

- `A ≤ |y| ≤ B`,
- `|y2| ≥ δ > 0` (here δ=1/4 in the finite checker),
- `dist(y, ±e1/2) ≥ η > 0` (here η=1/10),

so the point stays off the scaled pin sites and off the axial line where the leading `f_y` residual vanishes.

Use the same contact limit as the fixed-remote / matrix-cap sources:

    U_0 = (f, f_x, f_xx, f_xxx, f_y, f_xy)_0
        = (b, 0, 0, 12k, 0, 0).

Expand at `x = r y`. The leading raw witness residuals are

    f_y(ry)     = r · f_yy · y2 + O(r^2),
    f_x(ry)     = (r^2/2)·(12k y1^2 + 2 f_xxy y1 y2 + f_xyy y2^2) + O(r^3),
    f(ry) − b   = (r^2/2)· f_yy · y2^2 + O(r^3).

Hence the divided-difference scalings on this chart are

    p_y = 1,    p_x = 2,    p_height = 2.

Define the contact divided differences by stripping the displayed leading powers of `r`:

    J_grad_y = f_yy · y2,
    J_grad_x = 6k y1^2 + f_xxy y1 y2 + (1/2) f_xyy y2^2,
    J_height = (1/2) f_yy · y2^2.

With `|y2|≥δ>0`, `J_grad_y` isolates `f_yy`. The leading height row satisfies

    J_height = (y2 / 2) · J_grad_y

so height is **dependent at leading order**. Restoring the next Taylor term gives

    (f(ry)−b)/r^2 = J_height + r · H_height_next + O(r^2),

    H_height_next = 2k y1^3 + (1/2) f_xxy y1^2 y2 + (1/2) f_xyy y1 y2^2 + (1/6) f_yyy y2^3.

- pin-site pentatetracontic residuals `AQ_grad_next = (1/2658271574788448768043625811014615890319638528000000000)D⁴⁵f(z^44)`, `AQ_height_next = (1/119622220865480194561963161495657715064383733760000000000)D⁴⁵f(z^45)` with `z·AQ_grad_next = 45 AQ_height_next` (forty-sixth-and-higher jets open);
- pin-centered integrand power identity (net `r^3`: spatial 2 − grad 2 + hess 0 + height 3);

On `y2=0` with `|y1|` in the annulus and away from `±1/2`, the leading transverse `f_y` and height powers drop:

    f_y(r y1, 0) = (r^2 y1^2 / 2) f_xxy + O(r^3),
    f_x(r y1, 0) = (r^2/2)(12k y1^2) + O(r^3),
    f(r y1, 0)−b = 2k r^3 y1^3 + O(r^3 · other 3-jets).

Hence axial scalings are `p_x=2`, `p_y=2`, `p_height=3`, and the gradient Jacobian power is `r^4`. Contact rows:

    J_grad_y = (y1^2 / 2) f_xxy,
    J_grad_x = 6k y1^2,
    J_height = 2k y1^3.

Height is already independent at this axial leading order (cubic mark). Exact shared-gap-mark identity: `J_height = (y1/3) J_grad_x`; distinct scalings keep unmatched height `r` at 0.

After the same `U_0` constraints, the witness Hessian at `x = r y` has mixed leading powers:

    f_xx(ry) = r (12k y1 + f_xxy y2) + O(r^2),
    f_xy(ry) = r (f_xxy y1 + f_xyy y2) + O(r^2),
    f_yy(ry) = f_yy + O(r).

Contact entries after stripping those powers:

    H_xx_contact = 12k y1 + f_xxy y2,
    H_xy_contact = f_xxy y1 + f_xyy y2,
    H_yy_contact = f_yy.

Hence

    det H = r · H_xx_contact · H_yy_contact − r^2 · H_xy_contact^2 + O(r^2),

so the raw determinant contributes a leading factor `r^1`. The same leading powers hold on `C_axial` after dropping `y2` terms (`H_xx_contact = 12k y1`, `H_xy_contact = f_xxy y1`). The finite checker records these polynomials and the power; it does **not** evaluate the conditioned Gaussian expectation of the typed Hessian factor needed to finish the Kac–Rice integrand (`hessian_ledger_evaluated = false`).

On a declared chart the mesoscopic expected-count integrand contributes the exact powers

    r^(spatial) · r^(-grad_jac) · r^(hess_det) · r^(height_window)

with `spatial=2`, `height_window=3`, `hess_det=1`, and `grad_jac = 3` on `C_transverse` (resp. `4` on `C_axial`). The resulting net powers are

    C_transverse: 2 − 3 + 1 + 3 = 3,
    C_axial:      2 − 4 + 1 + 3 = 2

(the axial chart is area-measure zero inside the 2D annulus integral). This is a **power identity only**: it does not bound the contact Gaussian density factor, so it does not yet prove the PR7 target `γ_AB ≤ C r^(-d)`.

The exact local cubic family is

    f_r(x,z) = b-k*r^3/2 + 2*k*x^3 -(3/2)*k*r^2*x
               +(a/2)*z^2 +(q/2)*(x^2-r^2/4)*z
               +(c/2)*x*z^2 +(d/6)*z^3.

All six original endpoint constraints hold identically: heights b and b-k*r^3 at x=-r/2,+r/2, and both two-component gradients zero. At a=-2, k>0, q=c=d=0 the endpoint Hessians are diag(-6kr,-2) and diag(6kr,-2), so the types are an actual maximum and saddle.

At (x,z)=(r*u,r*v), exact differentiation gives

    f_x/r^2 = 6*k*(u^2-1/4)+q*u*v+(c/2)*v^2,
    f_z = r*a*v + r^2*((q/2)*(u^2-1/4)+c*u*v+(d/2)*v^2),
    f-b = r^2*a*v^2/2 + r^3*[
        k*(2*u^3-3*u/2-1/2)+(q/2)*(u^2-1/4)*v
        +(c/2)*u*v^2+(d/6)*v^3].

PR9 omits the -1/4 shift in its gradient rows and the corresponding cubic height terms. Its axial-gradient row differs by 3k/2 after division by r^2. That cannot be an O(r) remainder. At k=1,u=2,v=0 the true scaled gradient is45/2, not24, and the cubic height coefficient is25/2, not16. The same gradient discrepancy occurs in the declared transverse chart, for example (u,v)=(2,1/2).

Cause: f_x(0)=-(3/2)kr^2, f_z(0)=-qr^2/8 and f(0)=b-kr^3/2 vanish in an unscaled contact limit but do not vanish at the scale used to form these rows. Replacing finite-r pins by the contact target before rescaling is invalid here.

**Disposition: AMEND REQUIRED.** This is a counterexample to the displayed deterministic raw finite-r expansions, not a Gaussian sample counterexample and not a refutation of the persistence theorem. The preceding OpenAI review comments also repeated the uncorrected 6k*u^2 term; this exact calculation corrects that reviewer oversight. On A>1 the corrected drift6k*(u^2-1/4) is still nonzero, so the compensation-density question remains, with corrected input.

def family(mutant=None):
    """Cubic in x,y; all six original endpoint constraints hold exactly."""
    result = (b - k*r**3/2 + 2*k*x**3 - 3*k*r**2*x/2
              + a*y**2/2 + q*(x**2-r**2/4)*y/2
              + c*x*y**2/2 + d*y**3/6)

def test_old_dx_formula_has_nonvanishing_error(self):
        jx,*_=o.contact_rows()
        old=6*o.k*o.u**2+o.q*o.u*o.v+o.c*o.v**2/2
        self.assertEqual(old-jx,3*o.k/2)
        self.assertNotEqual(old,jx)

    def test_old_axial_dy_formula_has_nonvanishing_error(self):
        _,_,jy2,_,_=o.contact_rows()
        self.assertEqual(o.q*o.u**2/2-jy2.sub(v=0),o.q/8)

    def test_old_height_formula_has_missing_terms(self):
        *_,h3=o.contact_rows()
        old=2*o.k*o.u**3+o.q*o.u**2*o.v/2+o.c*o.u*o.v**2/2+o.d*o.v**3/6
        self.assertEqual(old-h3,3*o.k*o.u/2+o.k/2+o.q*o.v/8)

        minor=det3([[row.diff(name) for name in ('a','c','d')]
                    for row in (jx,jy1,j3)])

            self.assertEqual(f.diff('x').sub(x=xp,y=yp),0)

statements.text:
**Disposition: AMEND REQUIRED for the displayed deterministic pin/Taylor rows.**
This review does not refute the global Gaussian lifetime theorem, establish the full stochastic annulus estimate,
or award organizational independence. It provides an exact local counterexample to the stated algebraic expansion.

Let r>0, k>0, with longitudinal coordinate x and transverse coordinate z. Define

    F_r(x,z) = b - k*r^3/2 + 2*k*x^3 - (3/2)*k*r^2*x
               + (A/2)*z^2 + (a/2)*(x^2-r^2/4)*z
               + (c/2)*x*z^2 + (d/6)*z^3.

Direct substitution gives F_r(-r/2,0)=b, F_r(r/2,0)=b-k*r^3 and both gradients zero.
Its midpoint jet U_r tends to the source's U_0=(b,0,0,12k,0,0).
For A<0 and a=c=d=0 the left-pin Hessian is diag(-6kr,A), negative definite;
the right-pin Hessian is diag(6kr,A), a saddle. Thus even the required endpoint types
are compatible with the discrepancy.

The finite-r offsets are F_x(0)=-(3/2)kr^2 and F_z(0)=-a*r^2/8.
Although both vanish as r tends to zero, they do not vanish after the relevant divisions.

At (x,z)=r(y1,y2), exact differentiation gives

    F_x(ry)/r^2 = 6k*(y1^2-1/4) + a*y1*y2 + (c/2)*y2^2,
    F_z(ry) = r*A*y2 + r^2*[a*(y1^2-1/4)/2 + c*y1*y2 + d*y2^2/2],
    (F_r(ry)-b)/r^2 = A*y2^2/2 + r*H_next,
    H_next = -k/2 + 2k*y1^3 - (3/2)k*y1
             + (a/2)*(y1^2-1/4)*y2 + (c/2)*y1*y2^2 + (d/6)*y2^3.

The source's row `6k*y1^2+...` omits -3k/2. Its axial transverse row
`a*y1^2/2` omits -a/8. Its height coefficient omits -k/2-(3/2)k*y1-a*y2/8.
For r=1/10,k=1,y1=2,a=2,y2=0, the actual divided gradients are 45/2 and 15/4,
whereas the unshifted formulas give 24 and 4.

This is not a remainder-size disagreement: the scaled discrepancies are nonzero constants.
The invalid operation is substituting U_0 for the finite-r constraints before dividing by r^2/r^3.

For a family of C^5 functions with derivatives uniformly bounded on a common neighborhood,
with the exact same six pins, put h=r/2 and evaluate midpoint derivatives. Taylor expansion of
F_x(±h,0)=0 gives

    F_x(0) = -r^2*F_xxx(0)/8 + O(r^4),
    F_xx(0) = -r^2*F_xxxx(0)/24 + O(r^3).

The height difference is -kr^3; substituting the first relation gives
F_xxx(0)=12k+O(r^2). Averaging heights gives F(0)=b-kr^3/2+O(r^4).
Similarly F_z(0)=-r^2*F_xxz(0)/8+O(r^4) and F_xz(0)=O(r^2).
These identities reproduce the shifted leading longitudinal gradient and the shifted axial
transverse gradient. For the height next coefficient one must also carry the O(r^2)
F_xz(0) term at its correct order; it contributes only O(r^4) after evaluation at ry.
The stated uniform C^5 hypothesis is deterministic. It has not been verified here as a
uniform conditional Gaussian moment/density assertion over the project's parameter region.

Add the pin-preserving quartic term

    (D/24)*(x^2-r^2/4)^2.

All pins remain exact and F_xxxx(0)=D. On the axis the exact factorization is

    F_x(r*y1,0) = r^2*(y1^2-1/4)*(6k + r*D*y1/6).

The first free longitudinal residual in this example is order r^3. For fixed y1 away from
0 and ±1/2, cancellation requires D=-36k/(r*y1), outside a bounded-jet regime as r shrinks.
A determinant formed by varying k does not produce a density under a law that already fixes k.

A suitable next analytic lemma should establish the actual conditional mean and covariance of
(r^-3[F_x-E F_x], r^-2[F_z-E F_z]) uniformly on the stated axial chart.
If its covariance is bounded above and below and the first scaled target has size at least c/r,
the two-dimensional Gaussian density is at most C*r^-5*exp(-c'/r^2).
This follows from the standard Gaussian density formula and the diagonal Jacobian r^-5.
It is a CONDITIONAL implication: the covariance and drift hypotheses, typed Hessian factors,
height conditioning and extension to the thin belt are NOT discharged by this review.

statements.text:
| Source | Checked algebraic content | Imported / not checked here |
|---|---|---|
| F4-F5 | For a,b>=0, a+b>0, x>0, d=a+bx: d>0; if d^2 c=-abx, then c<=0 | x=exp(-t); differentiation; c actually equals the displayed second derivative |
| F10 | From (1-p)n=pm, the identity (1-p)^2 n-p^2 m=p(1-2p)m | Construction and normalization of binomial masses |
| F10 | Strict negativity for 1/2<p<1, m>0, n>=0; nonpositivity on the closed interval with m,n>=0 | Positivity of the particular binomial mass in the interior; induction across capacities |
| F11 | Real e>2 implies 0<3e-2<e^2 | e is Euler's number; exponential/logarithm monotonicity |
| Section 6 | Exact rational identities and positivity for 11/23520 and 26081/933120 | Exponential series tail bounds and the deduction about rho_star |

The strict '<0' in the source's F10 requires interior p<1 and a positive mass. At p=1 and a>=1, m=P(S=a)=0 and n=P(S=a+1)=0, so both sides are zero. `F10_STRICT_INTERIOR` and `F10_CLOSED_NONPOSITIVE` separate the two correct scopes; `M_STRICT_AT_P_ONE` records the false endpoint strengthening. The source application p_star=1-exp(-1) is interior, so this does not refute the full-price theorem. It is an additive precision note, not a silent edit to the frozen source.

Six deliberate false variants drop a>=0, drop b>=0, replace nonpositive curvature by strict negativity, reverse the recurrence sign, demand strictness at p=1, or omit the mass relation. Each has an explicit rational counterexample checked independently with Python Fraction and a solver SAT result for the negated false claim. Every positive statement also has an explicit rational premise witness and an additional SAT query, preventing acceptance solely from inconsistent hypotheses.

statements.text:
noncomputable def affinePotential (s a b c y : ℝ) : ℝ := c * foldPotential s (a*y+b)
noncomputable def plusPoint (s a b : ℝ) : ℝ := (s-b)/a
noncomputable def minusPoint (s a b : ℝ) : ℝ := (-s-b)/a
noncomputable def physicalSeparation (s a : ℝ) : ℝ := 2*|s|/|a|
theorem fold_hasDerivAt (s x : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (foldPotential s) (s^2-x^2) x := by
theorem fold_deriv (s x : ℝ) : deriv (foldPotential s) x = s^2-x^2 :=
theorem fold_second (s x : ℝ) : deriv (deriv (foldPotential s)) x = -2*x := by
theorem fold_critical (s x : ℝ) : deriv (foldPotential s) x = 0 ↔ x=s ∨ x= -s := by

theorem fold_nondegenerate (s : ℝ) :
    (deriv (deriv (foldPotential s)) s ≠ 0 ∧
     deriv (deriv (foldPotential s)) (-s) ≠ 0) ↔ s ≠ 0 := by

theorem fold_curvature (s : ℝ) :
    (deriv (deriv (foldPotential s)) s < 0 ↔ 0 < s) ∧
    (0 < deriv (deriv (foldPotential s)) (-s) ↔ 0 < s) := by

theorem affine_hasDerivAt (s a b c y : ℝ) : HasDerivAt (affinePotential s a b c)
    (c*a*(s^2-(a*y+b)^2)) y := by

theorem affine_deriv (s a b c y : ℝ) : deriv (affinePotential s a b c) y =
    c*a*(s^2-(a*y+b)^2) := (affine_hasDerivAt s a b c y).deriv

theorem affine_hasDerivAt_deriv (s a b c y : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (deriv (affinePotential s a b c)) (-2*c*a^2*(a*y+b)) y := by

theorem affine_second (s a b c y : ℝ) : deriv (deriv (affinePotential s a b c)) y =
    -2*c*a^2*(a*y+b) := (affine_hasDerivAt_deriv s a b c y).deriv

theorem affine_coordinates (s a b : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    a*plusPoint s a b+b=s ∧ a*minusPoint s a b+b= -s := by

theorem affine_critical (s a b c y : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    deriv (affinePotential s a b c) y=0 ↔ y=plusPoint s a b ∨ y=minusPoint s a b := by
theorem affine_orientation (s a b : ℝ) : plusPoint s a b-minusPoint s a b=2*s/a := by

theorem affine_distinct (s a b : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    plusPoint s a b ≠ minusPoint s a b ↔ s ≠ 0 := by

theorem affine_curvature (s a b c : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    deriv (deriv (affinePotential s a b c)) (plusPoint s a b)= -2*c*a^2*s ∧
    deriv (deriv (affinePotential s a b c)) (minusPoint s a b)=2*c*a^2*s := by

theorem affine_nondegenerate (s a b c : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    (deriv (deriv (affinePotential s a b c)) (plusPoint s a b) ≠ 0 ∧
     deriv (deriv (affinePotential s a b c)) (minusPoint s a b) ≠ 0) ↔ s ≠ 0 := by

theorem affine_curvature_sign (s a b c : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    (deriv (deriv (affinePotential s a b c)) (plusPoint s a b) < 0 ↔ 0<c*s) ∧
    (0 < deriv (deriv (affinePotential s a b c)) (minusPoint s a b) ↔ 0<c*s) := by

theorem separation_eq (s a b : ℝ) :
    |plusPoint s a b-minusPoint s a b|=physicalSeparation s a := by
theorem separation_nonneg (s a : ℝ) : 0 ≤ physicalSeparation s a :=
theorem separation_zero (s a : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) : physicalSeparation s a=0 ↔ s=0 := by

theorem affine_signed_gap (s a b c : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    affinePotential s a b c (plusPoint s a b)-affinePotential s a b c (minusPoint s a b)=
      c*(2*s)^3/6 := by

theorem affine_absolute_gap (s a b c : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    |affinePotential s a b c (plusPoint s a b)-affinePotential s a b c (minusPoint s a b)|=
      |c| * |a|^3*(physicalSeparation s a)^3/6 := by

theorem affine_increments (s a b c h : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    affinePotential s a b c (plusPoint s a b+h)-affinePotential s a b c (plusPoint s a b)=
      -c*(a*h)^2*(s+a*h/3) ∧
    affinePotential s a b c (minusPoint s a b+h)-affinePotential s a b c (minusPoint s a b)=
      c*(a*h)^2*(s-a*h/3) := by

theorem affine_local_signs (s a b c h : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hs : s ≠ 0)
    (hh0 : 0 < |h|) (hh1 : |h| < |s|/|a|) :
    c*s*(affinePotential s a b c (plusPoint s a b+h)-affinePotential s a b c (plusPoint s a b)) < 0 ∧
    0 < c*s*(affinePotential s a b c (minusPoint s a b+h)-affinePotential s a b c (minusPoint s a b)) := by

theorem affine_zero_degenerate (a b c : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    plusPoint 0 a b=minusPoint 0 a b ∧ plusPoint 0 a b= -b/a ∧
    deriv (affinePotential 0 a b c) (-b/a)=0 ∧
    deriv (deriv (affinePotential 0 a b c)) (-b/a)=0 := by

theorem affine_zero_increment (a b c h : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    affinePotential 0 a b c (-b/a+h)-affinePotential 0 a b c (-b/a)= -c*a^3*h^3/3 := by

theorem affine_zero_crossing (a b c h : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hh : h ≠ 0) :
    (affinePotential 0 a b c (-b/a+h)-affinePotential 0 a b c (-b/a))*
    (affinePotential 0 a b c (-b/a-h)-affinePotential 0 a b c (-b/a)) < 0 := by

theorem affine_constant_a (s b c y : ℝ) : affinePotential s 0 b c y=c*foldPotential s b ∧
    deriv (affinePotential s 0 b c) y=0 := by

theorem affine_constant_c (s a b y : ℝ) : affinePotential s a b 0 y=0 ∧
    deriv (affinePotential s a b 0) y=0 := by

def goodSample (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (ω : SourceMode d → ℝ) : Prop :=

statements.text:
def goodSet (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) : Set (SourceMode d → ℝ) :=
  {ω | goodSample d L ω}
theorem goodSet_measurable (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) : MeasurableSet (goodSet d L) := by

theorem goodSet_measure_one (d : ℕ) {L : ℝ} (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    sourceLaw d (goodSet d L) = 1 := by

def smoothLaw (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) : Measure (SmoothSample d L) :=
  (sourceLaw d).comap (sampleInclusion d L)

theorem sampleInclusion_measurePreserving (d : ℕ) {L : ℝ} (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    MeasurePreserving (sampleInclusion d L) (smoothLaw d L) (sourceLaw d) :=

theorem smoothLaw_isProbabilityMeasure (d : ℕ) {L : ℝ} (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    IsProbabilityMeasure (smoothLaw d L) := by

theorem observation_map_eq (d : ℕ) {L : ℝ} (hL : L ≠ 0)
    {E : Type*} [MeasurableSpace E] (X : (SourceMode d → ℝ) → E) (hX : Measurable X) :
    (smoothLaw d L).map (fun ω => X (sampleInclusion d L ω)) = (sourceLaw d).map X := by

theorem smoothSourceField_smooth (d : ℕ) {L : ℝ} (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (ω : SmoothSample d L) : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (smoothSourceField d L ω) :=

theorem smoothSourceField_finiteVector_hasGaussianLaw (d : ℕ) {L : ℝ} (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → (Fin d → ℝ)) :
    HasGaussianLaw (fun ω j => smoothSourceField d L ω (x j)) (smoothLaw d L) := by

theorem smoothSourceField_covariance (d : ℕ) {L : ℝ} (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (x y : Fin d → ℝ) :
    cov[fun ω => smoothSourceField d L ω x, fun ω => smoothSourceField d L ω y; smoothLaw d L] =
      sourceSpectralKernel d L (x - y) := by

theorem smoothTorusSourceField_smooth (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) [Fact (0 < L)]
    (ω : SmoothSample d L) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, Fin d → ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ (smoothTorusSourceField d L ω) := by

theorem smoothTorusSourceField_finiteVector_hasGaussianLaw (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ)
    [Fact (0 < L)] (n : ℕ) (q : Fin n → SourceTorus d L) :
    HasGaussianLaw (fun ω j => smoothTorusSourceField d L ω (q j)) (smoothLaw d L) := by

theorem smoothTorusSourceField_covariance (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) [Fact (0 < L)]
    (q p : SourceTorus d L) :
    cov[fun ω => smoothTorusSourceField d L ω q, fun ω => smoothTorusSourceField d L ω p;
      smoothLaw d L] =
      sourceSpectralKernel d L (torusRepresentative d L q - torusRepresentative d L p) := by

items.title: D1 Section 9 amendment v1 (D1-BOREL-KR-AMEND-20260925-v1): bounded-Borel marked pair Kac–Rice identity on U_eps via a C^2 regression kernel and functional monotone class, applied to the elder/type mark (E1), with height disintegration and exhaustion toward the diagonal

statements.text:
On \(U_\varepsilon\), the covariance of \(G_{x,y}\) is positive definite:
the relevant derivative evaluations occur at two distinct sites and are
linearly independent; the periodized field has strictly positive variance in
every Fourier mode. Compactness of \(U_\varepsilon\) then gives a uniform
positive covariance floor. The field is smooth, so the standard hypotheses for
the unweighted zero-count Kac–Rice formula hold.

Thus the unweighted expected number of ordered critical-point pairs in any
compact Borel \(A\subset U_\varepsilon\) is

\[
 \mathbb E N(A)
 =
 \int_A p_{G_{x,y}}(0)\,
   \mathbb E\!\left[
      |\det H_x\,\det H_y|\mid G_{x,y}=0
   \right]\,d(x,y).
 \tag{KR0}
\]

\[
 (z,v)\longmapsto \mathcal L(F_{z,v})
\]

is a Borel probability kernel on \(\mathcal F\), continuous against bounded
continuous cylinder functions. It is a concrete version of the regular
conditional law

\[
 \mathcal L(F\mid G_z=v).
 \tag{K2}
\]

Hence
\[
 \mathbb E\!\sum_{\substack{z\in U_\varepsilon\\G_z=0}} h(z,F)
 =
 \int_{U_\varepsilon}p_{G_z}(0)
   \,\mathbb E\!\left[
      |\det H_x\det H_y|\,h(z,F_{z,0})
   \right]dz
 \tag{KRc}
\]
for every bounded continuous cylinder \(h\).

The bounded continuous cylinder functions form a multiplicative algebra,
contain the constants, separate points, and generate the product Borel
sigma-algebra. The functional monotone-class theorem therefore gives

\[
 \mathcal H=L^\infty_{\mathrm{Borel}}
 (U_\varepsilon\times C^2(X)).
 \tag{M3}
\]

Thus (KRc) holds for **every bounded Borel field mark** on the compact
off-diagonal domain. This extension is our measure-theoretic step; it is not
attributed to a theorem that assumes lower semicontinuity of the final elder
mark.

For variable \(x\), the event \(\{d_f(x)>a\}\) is a countable union of strict
polygonal-path tests: use the fixed finite atlas, rational interior vertices,
rational clearances, and a short chart segment from the variable \(x\) to the
first rational vertex. Whenever a continuous path has strict clearance above
\(a\), it has such a rational approximation. Hence
\((x,f)\mapsto d_f(x)\) is Borel as an extended-real map.

Evaluation \((y,f)\mapsto f(y)\) is continuous on \(X\times C^2(X)\).
Therefore
\[
 \{(x,y,f):d_f(x)=f(y)\}
\]
is Borel. Hessian evaluation is continuous into the finite-dimensional
symmetric matrices, and the sets of negative-definite matrices and matrices of
a fixed nondegenerate Morse index are Borel (indeed open away from the
singular locus). Thus the product mark

\[
 h_{\rm elder}(x,y,f)
 =
 \mathbf1\{d_f(x)=f(y)\}
 \mathbf1\{H_x<0\}
 \mathbf1\{\operatorname{index}(H_y)=d-1\}
 \tag{E1}
\]
is bounded Borel on \(U_\varepsilon\times C^2(X)\).

By (M3), (KRc) applies to (E1). On the almost-sure Morse,
distinct-critical-value locus used in the parent proof, (E1) selects exactly
the ordinary finite superlevel elder-death partner; an essential maximum has
no strictly higher endpoint and hence is excluded.

Under the conditional kernel \(F_{z,0}\), the pair
\((F(x),F(y))\) is a nondegenerate two-dimensional Gaussian for distinct
\(x,y\) on \(U_\varepsilon\). Its mean, covariance and density vary
continuously in \(z\).

After the parent notation is restored, the selected density is the candidate
density multiplied by the tilted selection probability \(p_r\), with the
single determinant product already contained in \(W\). No second determinant
copy is introduced.

Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the domains increase to all distinct
ordered pairs. Nonnegative monotone convergence therefore extends the measure
identity to the off-diagonal pair space. This step imports the stated
near-diagonal integrability estimate; this amendment does not re-prove it.

This amendment establishes only the previously missing Section 9 interface,
conditional on the parent source's already stated finite-jet
nondegeneracy/smoothness and near-diagonal integrability inputs. It does not
convert those imported inputs into accepted theorems and does not alter any
scientific-status flag.

    (G : Fin b → Finset (Finset X))

Families and blocks: X is a finite type with decidable equality. D is a Finset of subsets with decreasing D, meaning ∅ ∈ D and D is closed under subsets (Definitions.lean:7-8). The block map is blk : X → Fin b; b = 0 and empty blocks are allowed. Palettes are P : Fin b → Finset (Fin K) with local demands k_i > 0 and k_i ≤ |P_i|.

Palette separation (Definitions.lean:46-49): for every minimalBad e meeting more than one block and every colour j, some block met by e lacks j in its palette.

Local covers: localGeneratorCover D blk i k_i G_i tests only subsets U of block i that are not k_i-decomposable in localFamily D blk i, the restriction of D to block i (Definitions.lean:30-33). The generator support hypothesis hgsub is carried in the signature; the amalgamation proof does not use it (Amalgamation.lean:100-102).

Budget theorems: these assume p ∈ [0,1]^X and c ≥ 0, plus the local price premise famPrice c (G i) ≤ phi(1 - localMass D blk p i). Here localMass is the block-coordinate mass of D's restriction to block i. The theorems do not assume c_v ≤ phi(p_v). The conclusion is coverCost D K c ≤ cappedHazard 1 (muOf D p), which equals min(1, -log mu) at positive mass and 1 otherwise.

- paletteSafety_iff states the equivalence for every finite U and every colouring f : X → Fin K.

statements.text:
theorem nnreal_weightedHolder {I Ω : Type} [Fintype I] [Fintype Ω]
    (q : Ω → ℝ≥0) (hq : ∑ a, q a = 1)
    (w : I → ℝ≥0) (hw : ∑ i, w i ≤ 1) (f : I → Ω → ℝ≥0) :
    (∑ a, q a * ∏ i, f i a ^ (w i : ℝ)) ≤
      ∏ i, (∑ a, q a * f i a) ^ (w i : ℝ) := by

theorem finner_productAverage {X A I : Type}
    [DecidableEq X] [Fintype A] [Fintype I]
    (q : X → A → ℝ≥0) (hq : ∀ x, ∑ v, q x v = 1)
    (xs : List X) (S : I → Finset X) (w : I → ℝ≥0)
    (hload : ∀ x, (∑ i, if x ∈ S i then w i else 0) ≤ 1)
    (f : I → (X → A) → ℝ≥0) (hf : ∀ i, functionDependsOn (S i) (f i)) :
    ∀ a, productAverage q xs (fun a => ∏ i, f i a ^ (w i : ℝ)) a ≤
      ∏ i, productAverage q xs (f i) a ^ (w i : ℝ) := by

theorem finner_tensor {I : Type} [Fintype I] [Nonempty A]
    (q : X → A → ℝ≥0) (hq : ∀ x, ∑ v, q x v = 1)
    (S : I → Finset X) (w : I → ℝ≥0)
    (hload : ∀ x, (∑ i, if x ∈ S i then w i else 0) ≤ 1)
    (f : I → (X → A) → ℝ≥0) (hf : ∀ i, functionDependsOn (S i) (f i)) :
    tensorAverage q (fun a => ∏ i, f i a ^ (w i : ℝ)) ≤
      ∏ i, tensorAverage q (f i) ^ (w i : ℝ) := by

theorem muOf_le_prod_restrictionMass_rpow {I : Type} [Fintype I]
    (D : Finset (Finset X)) (hD : decreasing D) (p : X → ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ v, 0 ≤ p v ∧ p v ≤ 1) (S : I → Finset X) (lam : I → ℝ)
    (hlam : ∀ i, 0 ≤ lam i)
    (hload : ∀ x, (∑ i, if x ∈ S i then lam i else 0) ≤ 1) :
    muOf D p ≤ ∏ i, (restrictionMass D p (S i)) ^ (lam i) := by

theorem restriction_fullGroundPriceBound (D : Finset (Finset X)) (hD : decreasing D)
    (g : Finset X) (hg : g.Nonempty) (hbad : g ∉ D) (p c : X → ℝ)
    (hp : ∀ v, 0 ≤ p v ∧ p v ≤ 1)
    (hc : ∀ v, 0 ≤ c v ∧ c v ≤ phi (p v)) :
    genPrice c g ≤ cappedHazard (1 / restrictionHazardStar D g) (restrictionMass D p g) := by

theorem witnessLoad_budget_of_productBound (D : Finset (Finset X))
    (hD : decreasing D) (K : ℕ) (G : Finset (Finset X))
    (hG : generatorCover D K G)
    (hnonempty : ∀ g ∈ G, g.Nonempty) (hbad : ∀ g ∈ G, g ∉ D)
    (p c : X → ℝ) (hp : ∀ v, 0 ≤ p v ∧ p v ≤ 1)
    (hc : ∀ v, 0 ≤ c v ∧ c v ≤ phi (p v)) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
    (hprod : 0 < muOf D p → muOf D p ≤ ∏ g ∈ G,
      (restrictionMass D p g) ^ (1 / (L * restrictionHazardStar D g))) :
    (0 < muOf D p → famPrice c G ≤ L * (-Real.log (muOf D p))) ∧
    (∃ H : Finset (Finset X), generatorCover D K H ∧
      famPrice c H ≤ cappedHazard L (muOf D p)) ∧
    coverCost D K c ≤ cappedHazard L (muOf D p) :=

theorem witnessLoad_budget (D : Finset (Finset X)) (hD : decreasing D)
    (K : ℕ) (G : Finset (Finset X)) (hG : generatorCover D K G)
    (hnonempty : ∀ g ∈ G, g.Nonempty) (hbad : ∀ g ∈ G, g ∉ D)
    (p c : X → ℝ) (hp : ∀ v, 0 ≤ p v ∧ p v ≤ 1)
    (hc : ∀ v, 0 ≤ c v ∧ c v ≤ phi (p v)) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
    (hload : ∀ v, (∑ g ∈ G, if v ∈ g then 1 / restrictionHazardStar D g else 0) ≤ L) :
    (0 < muOf D p → famPrice c G ≤ L * (-Real.log (muOf D p))) ∧
    (∃ H : Finset (Finset X), generatorCover D K H ∧
      famPrice c H ≤ cappedHazard L (muOf D p)) ∧
    coverCost D K c ≤ cappedHazard L (muOf D p) := by

theorem maximumWitnessLoad_budget (D : Finset (Finset X)) (hD : decreasing D)
    (K : ℕ) (G : Finset (Finset X)) (hG : generatorCover D K G)
    (hnonempty : ∀ g ∈ G, g.Nonempty) (hbad : ∀ g ∈ G, g ∉ D)
    (p c : X → ℝ) (hp : ∀ v, 0 ≤ p v ∧ p v ≤ 1)
    (hc : ∀ v, 0 ≤ c v ∧ c v ≤ phi (p v)) :
    (0 < muOf D p → famPrice c G ≤ maximumWitnessLoad D G * (-Real.log (muOf D p))) ∧
    (∃ H : Finset (Finset X), generatorCover D K H ∧
      famPrice c H ≤ cappedHazard (maximumWitnessLoad D G) (muOf D p)) ∧
    coverCost D K c ≤ cappedHazard (maximumWitnessLoad D G) (muOf D p) := by

def ThresholdStatement (k : ℕ) (L : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (Y : Type) [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] (p : ℝ), 0 < p → p < 1 →
    ∀ D : Finset (Finset Y), decreasing D →
      1 - 1 / (2 * (k : ℝ)) ≤ muOf D (fun _ => p) →
      ∃ G : Finset (Finset Y), generatorCover D k G ∧
        (∑ g ∈ G, (p / L) ^ g.card) ≤ (1 : ℝ) / 2

def PrizeStatement (q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (Y : Type) [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] (p : ℝ), 0 < p → p < 1 →
    ∀ A : Finset (Finset Y), 1 - 1 / (q : ℝ) ≤ muOf A (fun _ => p) →
      ∃ G : Finset (Finset Y), historicalGeneratorCover A q G ∧
        (∑ g ∈ G, p ^ g.card) ≤ (1 : ℝ) / 2

theorem decomposable_iff_union (D : Finset (Finset X)) (hD : decreasing D)
    (k : ℕ) (U : Finset X) : decomposable D k U ↔ unionDecomposable D k U := by

theorem generatorCover_iff_historical (D : Finset (Finset X)) (hD : decreasing D)
    (q : ℕ) (G : Finset (Finset X)) :
    generatorCover D q G ↔ historicalGeneratorCover D q G := by

theorem prizeStatement_iff_downset (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    PrizeStatement q ↔ DownsetPrizeStatement q := by

theorem cappedHazard_le_half_of_high_mass (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (m : ℝ)
    (hm : 1 - 1 / (2 * (k : ℝ)) ≤ m) : cappedHazard 1 m ≤ (1 : ℝ) / 2 := by

theorem threshold_cover_of_paletteCertificate (D : Finset (Finset X))
    (hD : decreasing D) (K : ℕ) (hK : 2 ≤ K) (L : ℝ) (hL : 1 ≤ L)
    (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1)
    (hmass : 1 - 1 / (2 * (K : ℝ)) ≤ muOf D (fun _ => p))
    (hcert : PalettePriceCertificate D K (fun _ => p) (fun _ => p / L)) :
    ∃ H : Finset (Finset X), generatorCover D K H ∧
      (∑ g ∈ H, (p / L) ^ g.card) ≤ (1 : ℝ) / 2 := by

theorem ThresholdStatement_of_certificates (K : ℕ) (hK : 2 ≤ K)
    (L : ℝ) (hL : 1 ≤ L)
    (hcert : ∀ (Y : Type) [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] (p : ℝ),
      0 < p → p < 1 → ∀ D : Finset (Finset Y), decreasing D →
        1 - 1 / (2 * (K : ℝ)) ≤ muOf D (fun _ => p) →
        PalettePriceCertificate D K (fun _ => p) (fun _ => p / L)) :
    ThresholdStatement K L := by

statements.text:
Let `M=(-r/2,0)`, `S=(r/2,0)`, and let `N` count critical points of any index at all heights. Under the original six pins and the endpoint weight `W_r/Z_r`, there are `K`, `C`, and `r_*>0` such that for `0<r≤r_*`,

```
E[N(M+r{0<|s|≤1/4})] ≤ C r^3,
```

and the same bound in the symmetric chart at `S`. The square `|p|≤K r`, `|q|≤K r` inside that disk contributes at most `C r^5`.
The disk `|s|≤1/4` reaches at most `ρ=3/4` and does not meet the reviewed annulus `ρ≥A>1`. The collar between `|s|=1/4` and `ρ=A` is not estimated.

The Gram comparison is the polynomial identity

```
576 Φ - ψ^2 = 143 β^4 + 2 r^2 α^2 β^2 ≥ 0,
```

so `Φ ≥ ψ^2/576`, with equality on the axis `β=0`, `α≠0`. Thus

therefore has `det Cov(H)` bounded below by a positive constant independent of `(α,β)` and of small `r`. It stays nondegenerate as `X→M` through the microdisk, including along `β=0`. The change of variables back to `(f_x,f_z)` has Jacobian `r^5 ψ`, so

```
p(grad f(X)=0) ≤ C / (r^5 ψ).
```

At `q=0` the first two values are `0` for every slope `t`, and

```
det(H_S/r) = 6 k C - 72 k^2 t^2.
```
Adding the three bands gives the microdisk bound `O(r^5)`.
The square, the cone, the steep strip, and the axis strip cover `0<|s|≤1/4`. The sum is `O(r^3)`. The symmetric chart at `S` has the drift `6 k p'(p'+1)` and the same bounds.

The claim as the source states it holds for d=2, under the six pins with 0<k_-≤k≤k_+ and the endpoint weight W_r/Z_r. There exist K, C, r_*>0 with E[N(M+r{0<|s|≤1/4})] ≤ C r^3 for 0<r≤r_*, where N counts critical points of any index at all heights. The same holds in the chart at S, and the square |p|,|q|≤Kr contributes at most C r^5.

- 576Φ−ψ^2=143β^4+2r^2α^2β^2 for the leading (S,T,Q) symbol Φ.

statements.text:
theorem side24_of_inputs (c24 : ℕ → ℝ)
    (href : ReferenceEnclosure) (hper : PeriodizationBound c24) : Side24Theorem c24 := by

def Side24Theorem (c24 : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Enclosed (c24 2) lower2 upper2 ∧ Enclosed (c24 3) lower3 upper3

def ReferenceEnclosure : Prop :=
  EnclosedClosed (cRef 2) refLo2 refHi2 ∧ EnclosedClosed (cRef 3) refLo3 refHi3

def PeriodizationBound (c24 : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  RelativeBound (c24 2) (cRef 2) ∧ RelativeBound (c24 3) (cRef 3)

noncomputable def coneMoment : ℕ → ℝ
  | 2 => 4 / 3
  | 3 => 29 / 6 - Real.sqrt 6
  | _ => 0

noncomputable def cRef (d : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Real.Gamma (7 / 6) * (3 / 2 : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 3) * coneMoment d
    / (2 * Real.sqrt 3 * Real.pi ^ (d - 1) * Real.sqrt Real.pi)
def Enclosed (c : ℝ) (lo hi : ℚ) : Prop := (lo : ℝ) < c ∧ c < hi
def EnclosedClosed (c : ℝ) (lo hi : ℚ) : Prop := (lo : ℝ) ≤ c ∧ c ≤ hi
def RelativeBound (c cref : ℝ) : Prop := |c / cref - 1| < (relBound : ℝ)

theorem enclosure_transfer {c cref lo hi r : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < cref) (hr1 : r < 1)
    (hlo : lo ≤ cref) (hhi : cref ≤ hi) (hr : |c / cref - 1| < r) :
    lo * (1 - r) < c ∧ c < hi * (1 + r) := by
theorem relBound_lt_one : (relBound : ℝ) < 1 := by
theorem oddBlock_minEigen_gt_third : (1 / 3 : ℝ) < 8 - Real.sqrt 58 := by
theorem exp_288_125_gt_ten : (10 : ℝ) < Real.exp (288 / 125) := by
theorem exp_neg_288_lt : Real.exp (-288) < 1 / 10 ^ 125 := by
theorem coneMoment_d3_bounds : 0 < coneMoment 3 ∧ coneMoment 3 < 29 / 6 := by
theorem cRef_pos (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 2 ∨ d = 3) : 0 < cRef d := by

statements.text:
/-- An explicitly bilinear, nonsymmetric form with a nonzero left radical. -/
def nonsymmetricForm (v w : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ := (v.1 - v.2) * (w.1 + w.2)

theorem nonsymmetricForm_bilinear (u v w : ℝ × ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
    nonsymmetricForm (u + v) w = nonsymmetricForm u w + nonsymmetricForm v w ∧
    nonsymmetricForm u (v + w) = nonsymmetricForm u v + nonsymmetricForm u w ∧
    nonsymmetricForm (a • v) w = a * nonsymmetricForm v w ∧
    nonsymmetricForm v (a • w) = a * nonsymmetricForm v w := by

theorem complementary_axes :
    (∀ z : ℝ × ℝ, z = (0, z.2) + (z.1, 0)) ∧
    (∀ a b : ℝ, (0, a) = (b, 0) → a = 0 ∧ b = 0) := by

theorem nonsymmetric_signed_axes_singular :
    (∀ t : ℝ, t ≠ 0 → nonsymmetricForm (0, t) (0, t) < 0) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, t ≠ 0 → 0 < nonsymmetricForm (t, 0) (t, 0)) ∧
    ((1, 1) : ℝ × ℝ) ≠ 0 ∧
    (∀ w : ℝ × ℝ, nonsymmetricForm (1, 1) w = 0) ∧
    nonsymmetricForm (1, 0) (0, 1) = 1 ∧
    nonsymmetricForm (0, 1) (1, 0) = -1 := by

/-- Literal criticality alone does not imply differentiability: fderiv defaults
to zero at a nondifferentiable point. This example is not claimed periodic. -/
theorem nonsmooth_literal_critical :
    (¬ DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun x : E 1 => ‖x‖) 0) ∧
    IsCriticalPoint 1 (fun x : E 1 => ‖x‖) 0 := by

/-- A half-open representative domain cannot supply compactness by itself. -/
theorem half_open_not_compact :
    ¬ IsCompact (Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1) := by
theorem closed_interval_compact : IsCompact (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) := isCompact_Icc

items.title: C294 conditional death-height attainment on the period-lattice torus quotient. Given local path connectivity of the closed death superlevel, a path from M to a strictly older critical point stays at or above superlevelBar_deathHeight g M and attains it (TorusCriticalAttainment.quotient_death_attainment, euclidean_death_attainment).

statements.text:
theorem quotient_death_attainment (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
    (g : E d → ℝ) (hsmooth : IsSmooth d g) (hperiodic : IsLPeriodic d L g)
    (hmorse : IsMorseDistinct d L g) (M : E d)
    (hnonessential : ¬ superlevelBar_isEssential g M)
    (hclosedLPC : LocallyPathConnectedSpace
      {q : torus_quotient d L hL //
        superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic q}) :
    ∃ Q ∈ quotientCriticalSet d L hL g,
      g M < descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic Q ∧
      ∃ γ : Path (torus_proj d L hL M) Q,
        (∀ t : unitInterval,
          superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic (γ t)) ∧
        ∃ t : unitInterval,
          descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic (γ t) = superlevelBar_deathHeight g M := by

theorem euclidean_death_attainment (d : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
    (g : E d → ℝ) (hsmooth : IsSmooth d g) (hperiodic : IsLPeriodic d L g)
    (hmorse : IsMorseDistinct d L g) (M : E d)
    (hnonessential : ¬ superlevelBar_isEssential g M)
    (hclosedLPC : LocallyPathConnectedSpace
      {q : torus_quotient d L hL //
        superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ descendedHeight d L hL g hperiodic q}) :
    ∃ y : E d, IsCriticalPoint d g y ∧ g M < g y ∧
      ∃ Γ : Path M y,
        (∀ t : unitInterval, superlevelBar_deathHeight g M ≤ g (Γ t)) ∧
        ∃ t : unitInterval, g (Γ t) = superlevelBar_deathHeight g M := by

statements.text: A deterministic update is constant on each cell of \(A_t\). If one available cell intersects two required cells of \(R_t\), no update can refine \(R_t\). That cell is an obstruction witness.

For a deterministic update \(M_t=f(A_t)\),

\[
H(R_t|M_t)\geq H(R_t|A_t).
\]

For task loss \(L\),

\[
\rho_L(R|M_t)\geq \rho_L(R|A_t).
\]

Every decision rule measurable with respect to \(M_t\) is also measurable with respect to \(A_t\). The information-loss defect is

\[
D_L(M_t;A_t)=\rho_L(R|M_t)-\rho_L(R|A_t)\geq0.
\]

For static exact support of required partitions \(P_1,\ldots,P_T\), memory must refine

\[
P_*=\bigvee_{t=1}^{T}P_t.
\]

For multiple tasks, minimize a vector of risks rather than assuming one scalar optimum. Memories can form MI–risk or multitask Pareto frontiers. Task mutual information and Bayes risk genuinely diverge in the included three-state observation model.

The deterministic specialized memories have minimax option risk \(0.25\). A 50/50 randomized mixture has distribution-level minimax risk \(0.125\). A realization-level adversary still obtains \(0.25\). Under expected loss, the robust memory is not automatically optimal; it becomes preferable only under specified hard constraints or noise regimes.

For independent binary symmetric channels with rates \(\alpha\) on \(x\) and \(\beta\) on \(z\), the specialized option risks are

\[
A_0=0.25\alpha+0.5(1-\alpha)\beta,
\qquad
A_1=0.25-0.25\alpha+0.5\alpha\beta.
\]

The full-observation floor is \((\alpha,\beta/2,\beta/2)\). A balanced specialized mixture has distribution-level minimax risk

\[
U_{\mathrm{dist}}=0.125+0.25\beta.
\]

A realization-level adversary obtains

\[
U_{\mathrm{real}}=0.25-0.25\alpha+0.5\alpha\beta.
\]

The exact gap is

\[
U_{\mathrm{real}}-U_{\mathrm{dist}}
=0.125(1-2\alpha)(1-2\beta).
\]

It vanishes when either channel is pure noise. Under balanced option uncertainty, the robust memory is expected-loss preferable to the balanced specialized mixture when \(2\alpha-\beta>1/2\).

Let \(\kappa=P(\text{both observations flip})\), with independence at \(\kappa=\alpha\beta\). Correlation changes posterior cell weights and can switch optimal decisions. The visibility gap is then piecewise rather than universally factorized.

For \(\alpha=0.2,\beta=0.3\), the independent formula predicts gap \(0.03\). The exact correlated model gives gap \(0\) at \(\kappa=0\), \(0.03\) at \(\kappa=0.06\), and \(0.05\) at \(\kappa=0.10\) and \(0.20\). The factorization is therefore independence-specific.
